subject: FY24 Budget Overview and Financial Planning
overview: The Committee of the Whole reviewed the Mayor's proposed Fiscal Year 2024 budget, focusing on capital planning, municipal staffing challenges, and the utilization of the city's $25 million free cash reserve.

items.title: Mayor’s FY24 Budget Presentation
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn presented a budget overview highlighting infrastructure investments in parks, fire headquarters design, and roads while noting the elimination of the city's structural deficit.

items.title: Medford Better Future Budget Plan
items.summary: Vice President Bears proposed a long-term financial strategy to address $31 million in projected capital needs for schools and streets and discussed charter amendments to formalize collaborative budgeting.

items.title: Municipal Staffing and Legal Services
items.summary: Councilors criticized the administration for failing to fill a dedicated council solicitor position and other vacancies, while the Mayor cited a regional shortage of qualified municipal professionals.

items.title: Free Cash and Revenue Analysis
items.summary: Finance Director Bob Dickinson explained that the $25 million free cash balance was generated through conservative revenue forecasting and salary savings from unfilled positions.

items.title: Motion for Written Responses
items.summary: Approved a motion requiring that all questions asked by the Council during budget hearings be answered by the administration in writing.

items.title: Finance and Auditing Department Review
items.summary: The committee reviewed the department's $723,871 budget, with discussion focusing on the estimated $2 million cost to modernize the city's aging accounting and payroll software.

items.title: Council on Aging Department Review
items.summary: Director Pam Kelly reported a 68% increase in senior center attendance over the past ten months and reviewed the department's $267,545 budget request.
